business_problem: Students who miss lectures struggle to reconnect new lessons with prior material when course information is spread across notes, recordings, slides, and readings, and lecturers need a reliable way to answer routine course questions and support exam preparation without replacing teaching.
solution_summary: Bar-Ilan University piloted a multilingual learning agent inside its Moodle learning platform to turn course repositories into searchable study support. Teaching staff upload recorded lectures, transcripts, presentations, articles, research papers, and recommended reading; those materials form the bot’s exclusive grounding corpus. KPMG and OpenApp developed the agent with Microsoft Copilot Studio, and Azure AI Services powers natural-language search, summarization, and quiz-style interactions over the course content. The service runs in BIU’s secure Microsoft Azure environment, keeping the experience inside the university’s managed cloud boundary. Students can ask questions in Hebrew, Arabic, or English to find lecture topics, generate summaries, and test themselves, while lecturers improve answer quality by refining course materials, adding fuller explanations, and feeding complete lecture transcripts into the system.

data_flow: Lecturers upload recorded lectures, transcripts, presentations, articles, research papers, and recommended reading into BIU's Moodle-based course environment. Microsoft Copilot Studio orchestrates an agent grounded only on that corpus, Azure AI Services processes student questions in Hebrew, Arabic, or English, and the resulting topic lookups, summaries, and quizzes are returned to students through Moodle inside BIU's secure Microsoft Azure environment.
integration_points: Articles, research papers, and recommended reading uploaded by BIU teaching staff
business_outcome: Students can search and summarize course content, generate self-tests, and study more independently; one student reduced post-lecture study time to about three hours from five to six. Lecturers report fewer routine and administrative questions and less exam anxiety among students. In one course, the lecturer said the average final score was three percentage points higher than in previous years, while noting the cohort may also have been stronger.

evidence_quotes: "In February, BIU piloted an AI agent on its Moodle learning platform that helps students search and summarize course materials using natural language queries, turning these vast resources into learning support."

"Powered by Azure AI Services and developed by KPMG and OpenApp using Microsoft Copilot Studio, the agent is grounded exclusively in course materials uploaded by BIU's teaching staff, including recorded lectures, transcripts, presentations and articles."
"The pilot covered 71 courses and about 2,400 students at BIU, one of Israel's leading public research universities with over 20,000 students in Ramat Gan, near Tel Aviv."
"Available in Hebrew, Arabic and English, the agent will be rolled out to another 100 courses in the first semester of the 2026/27 academic year."
"The agent operates in the university's secure Microsoft Azure environment."
"She now spends about three hours a day studying after lectures, compared with five to six hours previously."
"At the finals in August, the average score among his 50 or so students was three percentage points higher than in previous years."
